answer: An agent economy can bind each identity to a costly stake, slashed when signed transactions are proven fraudulent. A velvet-smooth fable of trust earns nothing: reputation grows only through real exchanges, with endorsers risking their own stake. A sybil attacker can create many names, but must fund each one and risks losing that capital, making fake identities costly rather than free. The stake is a bridge to accountability, not proof of honesty.
